title: Pin AGENTS.md byte-identical to its rendered source block before slice 2 edits it
action:
Build the net BEFORE the work it nets. Slice 2 edits `packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md` to add the D4 read-first mention and the D5 proof case. That block is rendered into `AGENTS.md`, the file agents actually load. Today nothing catches an edit to the block that was never regenerated: `rule_index_parity.rs` compares marker SETS only, so a body edit with identical markers passes, and CI has no regen-then-diff step (`rg -n regen .github/workflows/` returns nothing).

Write a new text-reading test file, `packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/agents_block_render_parity.rs`, that pins the two surfaces byte for byte.

Copy the shape of `rule_index_parity.rs` — a sibling in the same directory. It reads repo files as TEXT, imports no crate internals, and opens with a comment block explaining what is pinned and why. Match that: a reader six months from now must learn from the file itself why it exists.

What to pin: `AGENTS.md` carries a bee-owned block delimited by `<!-- BEE:START -->` and `<!-- BEE:END -->` (find them with `rg -n 'BEE:START|BEE:END' AGENTS.md` — two hits). The bytes between those markers must equal the rendered content of `packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md`. Read `onboard/merge.rs` for `fn merge_agents_content` and its marker grammar before you assume how the block is delimited — the marker match is whole-line anchored and there is a deliberate decoy case in its tests. Read `onboard/source.rs` for how the block template is located.

If rendering is not a plain copy — check whether bee:only markers or any runtime-specific render applies to this template — pin what IS deterministic and say in a comment exactly what is pinned and what is not. A test that over-claims is worse than one with a stated boundary.

The test must FAIL if someone edits `packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md` and does not run `bee dev regen`. Prove that: make a scratch edit to the block file, run the test, keep the red output, then revert the edit and run it green. Both outputs go in the cap proof. A parity test never observed failing is not known to work.

The failure message must name the fix — `bee dev regen` — not just report a mismatch. Follow how `rule_index_parity.rs` words its assertions.

This cell writes exactly one new file and edits nothing else. Do not touch AGENTS.md, AGENTS.block.md, or any skill.

truths: Editing packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md without running bee dev regen turns this test red
The test passes on the tree as it stands today
The failure message names bee dev regen as the fix

artifacts.substantive: a text-reading parity test with a header comment stating what is pinned and what is deliberately not; no crate-internal imports; no TODO stubs

key_links: the test locates the BEE:START/BEE:END block the same way merge.rs does, not by an ad-hoc string search
prohibitions: No edit to AGENTS.md or packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md is committed
No crate-internal import - this file reads repo text, like its sibling parity tests
The scratch edit used to prove the red is reverted before cap
